title: ArcCivs172: blacklist for input terrain and recovery of stalled construction
owner_requirement: Use a blacklist for input terrain rather than a whitelist of rocks/ores; remove arbitrary material prohibitions and fix repeated next-building placement failures.

ore_policy.before: Input terrain uses a curated whitelist of soils/rocks/plants and refuses other materials, including ordinary ores.
ore_policy.after: Input terrain is eligible by default. A short blacklist excludes bedrock and technical unbreakable/portal/marker blocks; native state excludes liquids/waterlogged and data-bearing/container cells. Actual ownership and protected-coordinate checks remain.
ore_policy.unchanged: Existing ownership, native before-images, physical support/headroom, liquids, bedrock no-mutation, admitted buildings and roads, stored objects, paid batches and complete34profile checks.
ore_policy.ore_mining_rewards: unchanged; terrain preparation does not become a mining reward
ore_policy.native_support_only: Reading or retaining a support cell destroys no material. Only actually replaced cells count as world-cell removal.
ore_policy.output_contract: Construction still emits its existing concrete DIRT/STONE/AIR recipe. Its output palette does not restrict input terrain and does not mint ore or valuables.

progression_scope: Reuse the existing bounded unpaid-plan recovery for the next missing ordinary level-one plot after a site refusal, including developed towns. Keep all actual buildings and accepted routes fixed; only adopt unpaid intent after fresh native proof and complete34forecast. Existing64attempt/oneforecast-per-retry/five-minute limits and ordinary payment remain. No new supply endpoint, starting grant, money reward, work-rate multiplier, receipt schema or manual resource grant. Actual material throughput after restored construction remains unmeasured.
assumptions: Calculator participants are settlements, not human players. Low/base/high1/4/5 represents affected settlements.

Activity is an explicit planning scenario, not telemetry or a hard cap:0/1/2 new construction sites per settlement-day, with0/16/128 actually replaced natural ore cells per site. This yields0/16/256 ore-cell events per settlement-day.
natural_ore_cells below are an ore-specific example of native world cells, not transferable ore items, Vault or premium tokens. They must never be converted to an invented money value.
A support cell left intact is excluded. New source permits some ore-bearing terrain; it does not grant mining drops or economic output for earthwork.

Actual counts depend on accepted blueprints and terrain. Restored ordinary construction/production can change physical item throughput and existing Auto deficit grants; zero indirect impact and self-sufficiency are not claimed.
Current SELL remains separate from the planned future/SHADOW SELL-to-contract transition. No shop, contract or price is changed.

flows.basis: One native ore cell is replaced without drops; no transferable item is issued.

live_verification: After delivery distinguish disk hash, JVM activation and actual next-building paid progress. No direct world edits, forced arrival or manual grants are used to pass acceptance.
scope: Input policy applies to unprotected ordinary block materials, not only ores. Valuable block material alone is not an authority rule. Existing cut/fill no-drop accounting and physical budgets remain; actual modified-cell and later production throughput are not yet measured.
blacklist_economic_scope: The calculator isolates the observed ore incident. Other newly eligible ordinary native materials can also be replaced without drops; counts/value are unknown and not converted to currency. All these writes remain in the existing paid/native receipt; no item reward or manual grant is introduced.
